listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 622

An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Ps Cn for 13
div.ab: Si aduena uel peregrinus, qui de longinquo uenerit, sit calumniatus de foresta, et talis est sua inopia, ut non possit habere plegios, ad primam calumniam, quali nullus Anglus iudicari potest, tunc subeat captionem regis et ibi expectet, quousque uadat ad iudicium ferri et aque.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 622 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: If a stranger or foreigner who has come from afar is accused concerning the forest, and his poverty is such that he cannot have pledges, at the first accusation, in such a way as no Englishman can be judged [?], then let him undergo the king's arrest and wait there until he goes to the ordeal of iron and of water.
